nodes.note: Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, began 2014 as the Co-op Education Project, renamed 2019, incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer.

nodes.note: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.

props.address: 1220 N Forest St and 315 Westerly Rd, Bellingham
props.people: Lisa Sedlar — CEO; Lydia Cox — Marketing & Outreach Director; Annabelle Rosborough — Board Administrator

nodes.note: PO Box 244, Acme; farm stand at 2399 Mt Baker Hwy. Farmer-owned (Whatcom and Skagit ranchers), established 2016 (organising from 2012). USDA-inspected mobile slaughter. Founding board: Buttin' Grove Farm, Matheson Farms, Hannegan Farm and Home. Cascade Cooperatives member.

props.address: Farm stand 2399 Mt Baker Hwy, Bellingham; PO Box 244, Acme WA 98220

edges.note: Supplies grass-fed beef — The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.
edges.label: Supplies grass-fed beef

edges.note: Co-op development help (USDA grant) — Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell membership and equity shares. Source: agbizcenter.org.
